\section{Conclusion}

We constructed a global arbitrary-order enclosure calculus for the $\SU$
heat-kernel action.  Pairing images before differentiation makes the identity
regular; time-maximized image bounds control the transition chart; positive
odd-image pairs and a principal-pair lower bound control the cut chart.  The
antipodal formula displays the $t^{-5/2}$ Morse--Bott prefactor and the
associated loss of convexity.  Exact normalization yields a direct Haar-tail
theorem, while the order-eight rational validation supplies reproducible
numerical instances of the analytic bounds.

The result closes a finite representation problem: spectral and image
descriptions now exchange normalization, derivative information, and endpoint
geometry with explicit losses on the full class interval.  For lattice gauge
theory it provides a sharp one-plaquette small-field input.  Transporting that
local rigidity through a dependent, gauge-invariant multiscale measure
remains a separate problem.
